items.title: OpenAI: AI use by its own researchers keeps rising exponentially
items.takeaway: OpenAI shares new data: researchers' AI use keeps rising exponentially, agents complete longer tasks, humans stay central, and researchers spend more time on safety.
items.soWhat: How a frontier lab uses agents today previews how expert teams will work next.

items.title: ThePrimeagen: Sol set up sign-in across five services in 5 minutes
items.takeaway: ThePrimeagen told Sol to use his computer to create tokens for Cloudflare, YouTube, Twitch, Kick and X and make sign-in work locally and in production.
items.soWhat: Agents that operate your computer can now clear tedious setup work in minutes.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon models a 3D lab scene through Blender MCP
items.takeaway: Sundar Pichai shows Gemini 4 Neon 3D-modeling a photorealistic lab simulation in Antigravity via Blender MCP.
items.soWhat: Design tools are becoming something agents drive directly, not just something people click.

items.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Neon for engineering, knowledge work and science
items.takeaway: Gemini 4 Neon sits between Carbon and Hydrogen and rolls out today in the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Gemini for business and paid AI Pro and Ultra.
items.soWhat: Google's fourth Gemini 4 model this month keeps the price and quality race moving.

items.title: David Sacks: Anthropic sells 'closing the loop' on its IPO roadshow
items.takeaway: Sacks argues Anthropic is racing toward recursive self-improvement faster than any lab. The Atlantic calls it the reluctant winner; Gary Marcus asks if the IPO is a bad bet.
items.soWhat: Anthropic's IPO is turning its safety stance into a public debate over speed and risk.

items.title: Amjad Masad: Replit Missions shows how your agents coordinate
items.takeaway: Masad notes the OpenAI and Hugging Face incident exposed message boards where agents talk, and says Replit Missions lets you see that coordination.
items.soWhat: When agents talk to each other, teams need to see those conversations to trust the work.

items.title: Benaich: Abundant Labs launches a test for self-improving models
items.takeaway: Nathan Benaich says Abundant Labs launched FrontierRSI, which tests whether a model can achieve recursive self-improvement.
items.soWhat: Self-improvement is moving from debate to something investors want measured.

items.title: The Verge asks what Nvidia is without Jensen Huang in charge
items.takeaway: The Verge, on Nvidia's earnings: 'What is Nvidia without AI's sugar daddy in charge?'
items.soWhat: Leadership risk at the main AI chip supplier is now part of the compute story.

items.title: Benaich: what would a genius bar for AI look like?
items.takeaway: Benaich imagines giving a small business owner, a busy family or a healthcare provider an hour with someone who shows them what AI can do for their own work.
items.soWhat: Adoption may hinge on hands-on help with real work, not better models alone.

items.title: Microsoft and Perplexity both pitch AI as the OS for work
items.takeaway: Nadella says Salesforce is coming to Copilot 'as we build Copilot as the OS for work'. Perplexity puts Teammates and Multiagent on mobile, calling it 'a mini workOS'.
items.soWhat: The fight is shifting from best model to which assistant owns the daily workspace.

items.title: LangSmith now shows what each merged PR from coding agents costs
items.takeaway: A new LangSmith dashboard pulls traced coding agents into one view across harnesses and providers, links PRs to threads, and shows spend that never led to a PR.
items.soWhat: Leaders can finally tie coding-agent spend to shipped work, not just token bills.

items.title: LangChain: Deep Agents passes 50 million downloads
items.takeaway: LangChain says its Deep Agents framework has passed 50 million downloads.
items.soWhat: Open agent frameworks are becoming standard parts of the builder toolkit.

items.title: OpenAI explains how the Codex sandbox works
items.takeaway: OpenAI published 'Inside the Codex sandbox'. Simon Willison's new post covers external sandboxes for coding agents.
items.soWhat: Where agents run code decides how much damage a mistake can do.
